title: Bowel obstruction and ileus in the hospital
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the bowel obstruction or ileus (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/15/2026
Reason for Admission: Abdominal pain and nausea

Vitals:
Temperature: 98.6 F
Heart Rate: 78 bpm
Blood Pressure: 132/84 mmHg
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 97% on room air

Recent Labs:
WBC: 9.2 x 10^9/L
Hemoglobin: 13.4 g/dL
Hematocrit: 40%
Creatinine: 1.1 mg/dL
eGFR: 72 mL/min/1.73m2
Electrolytes: Sodium 138 mEq/L, Potassium 4.1 mEq/L

Review of Systems:
The patient reports abdominal discomfort and intermittent nausea. He denies fever, chills, chest pain, or shortness of breath. He denies changes in bowel habits or urinary symptoms.

Social History:
The patient resides in a private residence with his spouse. He is a retired engineer and is a former smoker (quit 20 years ago). He denies alcohol or illicit drug use.

Family History:
Father had hypertension. Mother had type 2 diabetes. No family history of significant gastrointestinal disease.

Hospital Course:
The patient is an 86-year-old man who presented to the emergency department with progressive abdominal pain and associated nausea. Upon physical examination, he exhibited mild tenderness in the mid-abdomen. Imaging and clinical assessment confirmed a partial small bowel obstruction. The specific cause of the obstruction was not identified during the course of his stay. Management focused on conservative measures, primarily bowel rest and intravenous fluid resuscitation. During the hospitalization, the patient tolerated a clear liquid diet well and showed significant improvement in abdominal comfort. The obstruction resolved without the need for surgical intervention. He was stable for discharge once he was able to tolerate oral intake.

Discharge Diagnoses:
Partial small bowel obstruction

Discharge Medications:
1. Ondansetron 4mg as needed for nausea
2. Multivitamin daily
3. Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with his primary care physician in one week for a routine check-up and to monitor his recovery from the abdominal event. He was instructed to seek immediate medical attention if he experiences worsening pain, vomiting, or fever.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, MD
05/15/2026
explanations: Partial intestinal obstruction, cause not stated: K56.600 (HCC 78).
